item.title: How Dolly Parton's literacy work affected Indigenous communities in Australia
item.description: In Australia, the queen of country music, Dolly Parton, is being remembered for her work in advancing children's literacy, particularly in Indigenous communities.
item.content:encoded: In Australia, the queen of country music, Dolly Parton, is being remembered for her work in advancing children's literacy, particularly in Indigenous communities.

item.title: The Clancy jury continues to deliberate
item.description: The jury in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the mother charged with murdering her three children, said it's not yet come to an unanimous decision. The judge has urged them to keep trying.

item.title: Why the Supreme Court's ballroom ruling could matter beyond the ballroom
item.description: Georgetown Law professor Stephen Vladeck explains the separation-of-powers questions raised by the Supreme Court's decision on the White House ballroom.

item.title: USPS 'carefully reviewing' whistleblower claim on plan for Trump's mail in voting order
item.description: A whistleblower says the U.S. Postal Service is rushing out an online system for President Trump's push to restrict mail voting that could "derail" the midterm election if courts allow it to proceed.

item.title: A makeover for college: No gym, no meal plan and two years of work
item.description: A new model in Vermont emphasizes hands-on learning while stripping away frills like gyms and meal plans that increase costs. Other newly created institutions are also reimagining college.
